description: The house lanes a Kalshi market brief may turn into an allocator opportunity (src/kalshi-market-brief.mjs allocatorOpportunities). A lane is a measured rule, not a forecast: it names the market set it applies to, the quote band it needs, and the win probability it is allowed to claim. The desk's own policy files remain the authority for stake sizing; this file only decides whether research hands the desk a candidate.

feeModel.basis: Kalshi quadratic taker fee, ceil(rate * P * (1 - P) * 100) cents on a 10-lot, per contract. Series fee_multiplier scales it.

weather-tail-premium.applies: KXHIGH*/KXLOW* daily-temperature series declared in temperature-markets.json
weather-tail-premium.evidence: data/records/2026-10-03-kalshi-temperature-tail-backtest/README.md: at model p <= 0.01 (high) / 0.005 (low) and ask <= 0.05, 0 of 422 high and 1 of 448 low certified tails settled yes.

published-series-favorite.applies: daily markets settled on a published series (AAA gas, EIA diesel): families in kalshi-category-base-rates.json
published-series-favorite.winProbability: lower 95% Wilson bound of the family's YES rate at the nearest measured horizon at or above hours-to-close
published-series-favorite.evidence: content/config/kalshi-category-base-rates.json families: near-close favorites settle YES 99.8-100% (AAA gas n=2,100-2,500 per horizon).

leads.Mentions: Longshots (YES ask <= 5c) are underpriced near close in the sample (1 of 6 settled YES at 6h, 1 of 7 at 2h) while favorites are overpriced (9 of 11 at 6h). n is too small to emit an opportunity; the brief carries the band as a base rate and the Koios article says so.
